title: Proper closed bound for supports of a bounded tensor
statement: Let f:X -> S be a locally finite-type scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let E be any object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let G be a bounded complex of O_X-modules whose every term has support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. There exists a closed subset Z of X proper over S such that for every integer i the nonzero-stalk locus of H^i(E tensor^L G) [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] is contained in Z. This does not assert that these cohomology supports are closed. No perfection, coherence, relative flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: 0DJQ: support hypothesis in the application of 08EV; 01AT; 09MQ (4); 03GN

proof.text: Choose for each term its closed support Z_n from HasSupportProperOver; the support equality uniquely determines this closed subset. Extract a,b bounding G. Reindex the finite subtype of integers in Finset.Icc a b by Fin(card I), and let T be the supremum of the resulting closed subsets. Apply isClosedSubsetProperOver_union_preimage, clause (1), to obtain properness of T over f, including the empty interval.

Every term support is contained in T. For n in the interval use le_iSup. Outside the interval G.X n is zero by the bounding hypothesis; forgetting to the abelian presheaf and taking stalks preserves zero, so its stalks are subsingletons and its support is empty.

On U=X minus T, section_ext and the subsingleton stalks make the identity of each over-site restricted term zero. Pass through Modules.overEquiv U, and use componentwise HomologicalComplex.Hom.ext to prove the restricted complex is zero. Q preserves zero; mapDerivedCategoryFactors gives that the derived restriction of Q(G) is zero. Derived tensor commutes with this restriction by derivedTensor_openRestriction_iso_universes; tensorLeft preserves zero by the canonical monoidal preadditive derived structure. Thus the restricted tensor is zero.

The exact restriction R commutes with derived homology by mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. Hence R(H^i(E tensor Q(G))) is zero. Its stalk at a point y of U is a subsingleton. Compose Modules.overFunctorEquiv U with Modules.restrictStalkNatIso U.ι y to identify this stalk with the original stalk at x. For x outside T this contradicts membership of x in the nonzero-stalk locus. Pair this support containment with the properness of T.

proof_origin.place: Support verification, using finite unions (0CYR), locality of derived tensor (08DX), and exact open restriction (015F); Lean proof by Y2, 2026-10-13.

lean.statement:
theorem boundedComplex_tensor_proper_support_bound
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hGb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hGproper : ∀ n : ℤ, Modules.HasSupportProperOver f (G.X n)) :
    ∃ Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X, IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Z ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ,
        {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton
          ((Modules.presheaf (X := X)
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) i).obj
                (E ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G))).stalk x)} ⊆ (Z : Set X)
